messages:
miriam: Quick idea - prototyping a tiny span coalescer at ingest to collapse very short sibling spans (mobile pings, helper RPCs) to reduce cardinality and smooth billing spikes. Want to surface tradeoffs before I build.

devon: High level sounds good. How do you decide which spans to coalesce?

miriam: Candidate rule: same trace_id + parent_id + effective_route, name in configurable whitelist, start times within a sliding window (150-400ms). Emit a synthetic span with merged_count, raw_sum_cost, smoothed_cost, merge_bucket and merge_window_ms.

anish: Immediate risks: 1) hides retry/hedging patterns, 2) distorts tail/percentile metrics since you remove individual samples.

sam: Also problematic for streaming/gRPC flows where many short spans are semantically distinct.

miriam: Agreed. Safety rules I'm proposing: whitelist-only, never merge if error=true, streaming=true, duration>1s, dont_merge flag present, or caller identity/downstream endpoint differs. Also cap merge_refs list length to avoid bloat.

katie: For billing: do we sum token/byte costs or compute a smoothed value? If we just sum, minute-level retry storms can spike a customer's bill.

miriam: We'll keep raw_sum_cost for audit and compute smoothed_cost used by dashboards/nearline billing: smoothed = min(raw_sum, baseline + alpha * sqrt(raw_sum)). Baseline is per-tenant+route and only created when traffic > threshold (1 rps for 60s). Otherwise fallback to global baseline.

devon: Baseline lifecycle matters: TTL and decay when traffic drops. Also baseline metadata should be traceable for debugging.

sam: What about sampling? If sampling happens after ingest, merged_count/raw_sum must be preserved and upsampled.

miriam: Merge happens before sampling. Sampled traces include merged_count and raw_sum; billing pipeline multiplies raw_sum by sampling_inverse when available and marks estimates if missing.

anish: Add merge_bucket/version and merge_reason fields so queries can filter. Also include merge_id list referencing original span IDs (bounded).

miriam: Example emitted fields: merged:true, merged_count:4, merge_bucket:"coalesce-short-v1", merge_reason:"idempotent-helper", merge_window_ms:250, raw_sum_cost:120, smoothed_cost:85, merge_refs:["a1","a2","a3"]. We'll cap merge_refs length and drop detailed refs behind a feature flag.

katie: Billing pipeline needs to accept raw_sum + sampling factor and an estimate flag; product wants transparency on whether smoothing was applied to chargeback numbers.

devon: Ops plan: canary in one region for two weeks. Measure: ingest CPU, storage delta, query fidelity (compare top-100 flows percentile deltas), billing delta, and false-positive merge rate.

miriam: Action items:
- miriam: prototype ingest coalescer at gateway with whitelist + safety rules + metadata.
- devon: design per-route/tenant baseline service with TTL/decay and thresholds.
- katie: validate billing pipeline can consume raw_sum + sampling inverse; add estimate flag and audit markers.
- anish: build dashboards comparing percentiles and counts pre/post.
- sam: identify candidate non-sensitive routes/customers for canary and help with toggles.

ops-bot: created ticket INF-8340 span coalescing prototype (epic: obs-cost-optim).

sam: Please ensure route/customer feature-flag and ability to toggle on/off per route.

miriam: Will add feature flags and a short RFC with examples and sample queries tomorrow. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
